Meeting: Product/Eng sync — self-service password reset
Attendees: Priya (Product), Marcus (Eng lead), Dana (Support lead), Sam (Security)

Priya: Support ticket volume for password resets is up 40% this quarter. Right now
every reset goes through a support agent manually verifying identity over email,
which is slow and doesn't scale. I want to scope a self-service flow.

Dana: Agreed, it's our #2 ticket category. Average resolution time is 6 hours because
we're waiting on email round-trips. A self-service flow could cut that to minutes.

Marcus: Technically straightforward — email a time-limited reset link, same pattern
as most SaaS products. Question is what identity verification we require before
issuing the link, and whether SSO users go through the same flow.

Sam: SSO users should NOT get a password reset flow at all — their password is
managed by the identity provider, not us. If someone on SSO hits "forgot password"
we need to detect that and redirect them to their IdP's own reset flow instead.

Dana: We'll need a way to distinguish SSO vs. local accounts before the flow even
starts, then. Right now the login page doesn't ask for that up front.

Marcus: We can look up the account by email first, check if it's SSO-provisioned,
and branch from there. Adds a step but avoids a confusing dead end for SSO users.

Priya: What about rate limiting? We don't want this to become a way to spam
someone's inbox or enumerate valid accounts.

Sam: Strong opinion here — cap it at 3 reset requests per account per hour, and
don't reveal in the response whether the email exists or not. Same response either
way, to prevent account enumeration.

Marcus: That's an easy add on the endpoint. Open question: does the rate limit
apply per account or per IP too? A single IP hammering many different emails is a
different attack pattern than one account being spammed.

Priya: Let's flag that for security review rather than deciding here.

Dana: One more thing — once someone resets their password, should we force
logout of all their other active sessions? If an account was compromised, leaving
old sessions alive defeats the purpose of the reset.

Marcus: We can do that, yes. Reasonable default is to session-revoke everywhere
except the device doing the reset.

Priya: Good. Let's write this up — I think this is BRD-ready. Rough scope: self-
service reset for local accounts, SSO detection and redirect, per-account rate
limiting, and session revocation on successful reset. IP-based rate limiting is an
open question for security to weigh in on.
